guide.title: What this type needs
guide.rss:
News from the site's RSS or Atom feed.
• The feed is usually at /feed or /rss, or linked as “RSS” in the site footer.
• Site URL is the home page on the same domain as the feed.
guide.sitemap:
A news sitemap (Google News sitemap): every link has a news:title.
• Look for it in the site's robots.txt, a “Sitemap: …news….xml” line.
• A regular sitemap or a sitemap index won't work: no articles will be found.
guide.html:
A public Telegram channel.
• The channel must be public: t.me/s/channel_name opens without signing in.
• Page address: https://t.me/s/channel_name; site URL: https://t.me/channel_name.
• A regular site without RSS can't be added this way: each needs its own profile from a developer (cbf is an example).
guide.calendar:
Official public holidays of a country from an open API.
• Pick the profile for the API and paste the example address with your country code.
• {year} is filled in automatically: the current year, and the next one near year end.
• Site URL is on the same domain as the calendar address. Holidays for the next 3 days are taken.
guide.manual:
Articles from this site are only added by hand, with “Add link”.
• No feeds; the source is not polled.
• Only the site URL is needed: added articles are matched to the source, and its trust level, by domain.
guide.after: After creating, press “Test now” at the bottom of the page: it shows which articles would be found, saving nothing.

how.title: How importance is scored
how.not_sports: Not about sport (no sport, clubs or competitions found) — Off-topic, no points.
how.rules: Each signal below: a listed word in the headline gives weight × 2, only in the text — weight × {body}. Each signal counts once.
how.competition: A competition from the directory adds its priority (−1 to 2) or the weight from Custom competition weights.
how.team: A club with the top priority in the directory: +{n}.
how.levels: Total from {high} — High, from {medium} — Medium, below — Low.
how.event: An event gets the highest importance among its articles; a priority −1 competition or likely old news lowers it one level. A level set by an editor by hand is kept.
